about: First-time win-rate bands for levels 1 to 5, per pillar and per bot, from the Advisor's targets. Hero stats are not nerfed to meet them. A figure that misses its band can only be listed in known_misses with its measured value: CI then fails if it gets worse or comes back inside its band.
measure: HoldfastCurve.climb: a first-time player who buys the cheapest star and gold nodes between runs, wears the gear found, places posts and replays a level until it wins. A rate is first-attempt wins over the players who reached the level. Bots: average (reacts in 6 ticks, special every decision), poor (18 ticks, special every second decision).

hard.about: First-attempt win rate of each level's Hard replay for the average bot, played once right after the level is first cleared (the same players as the climbs). The modifier changes how the level is played (faster, tougher or more dangerous monsters, a frailer Keep, leaner pay), so Hard is a different fight and not the same one with bigger numbers. The bands are the first measurement with room each way; the Advisor and the Head of Engineering set the final ones.

tree.how: the average bot plays on from the end of the tutorial, spending stars and gold between runs, playing each cleared level's Hard replay once and replaying its latest level; the hours are the play time until it owns every gold node its Hero can reach (the whole budget if it never does), and a dry run is a return to the tree with nothing affordable. The stars the five levels pay cannot fill the tree, so the star side is reported, not judged, until more levels exist.

pillar_levels_note: Which levels each pillar is judged on (a pillar not named is judged on all five). The Dusk Mage unlocks at the level 5 boss and the Tideblade at the next biome boss, so both are tuned to the biomes they unlock into (Advisor view 2026-10-30, Head of Engineering decision). Gull Rock, the hardest level that exists, stands in for them. WIDEN THE SCOPE when a later biome exists. The gate fails if a pillar's scope is empty. Levels outside a scope are reported as not played by that pillar yet.

fork_gap.how: per level and pillar, the first-time win rate of the Volley side against the Sniper side (average bot, 12 players each)

special_gap.how: per pillar, the first-time win rate of the average bot with its special less the same players with it never pressed; the mean over the levels judged is at most 40 points (the special is worth pressing, not required), and the first level is winnable without it

one_post.how: the Dusk Mage with only the first castle slot bought, average bot, 12 players

known_misses_note: A pinned miss may not get worse, and CI fails if it comes back inside its band (delete the pin then). Build 12a (HF-M2-28) removed every pin that levels and data could fix and pinned what remains, each with its cause. flare_archer/special_gap/mean is fixed by Keeper's Habit (HF-M2-63): a player who never presses the special saves up for it (300 gold after Light feet, a few runs of Outpost) and then has it firing on its own, and the gap is now the special pressed against never pressed with the Habit (about 35 points, in band); its pin is deleted. flare_archer/no_special/outpost: no node can be bought before the first fight (the tutorial pays 150 gold), so a player who never presses the special and has not bought the Habit still loses Outpost; the guided first press (HF-M2-63) teaches the button before that fight. flare_archer/fork_feel/tidewrack_cove: the two Archer sides play within 3% of each other at Tidewrack Cove; the fork nodes are rebalanced with HF-M2-63. dusk_mage/average/gull_rock, tideblade/special_gap/mean and tideblade/poor/gull_rock: Levels 1 to 5 are shared by all three pillars, so Gull Rock cannot be tuned for the Dusk Mage and the Tideblade without taking the Flare Archer out of band, and monsters must not depend on the Hero picked; they are tuned when the biome they unlock into exists. The three tree/hours pins (HF-M2-68, re-measured with HF-M2-70): the gold nodes are priced from the gold a run pays where each tier opens (content/base/gold_tiers.json) and no node waits more than 3 dry runs, and with Hard replays counted the average bot still owns every gold node its Hero can reach in about an hour of play (1.2 h, 1.4 h and 1.2 h with the HF-M2-71 salvage), against the 3 to 4 hours the Advisor sets for the whole tree. The tree has about 40 gold nodes and the later biomes add the rest, so hours and the 3-run limit cannot both hold on this tree; the 3-run limit is kept and the hours are pinned, which may not fall further, and CI fails once they reach the band. More nodes come with the later arms. HF-M2-71 (salvage a quarter of a run's gold, not a whole run): the average bot has only the five levels to replay, so it plays Gull Rock for about 1,300 gold a run, and the dearest nodes (the tier that opens in biome 2, priced for about twice that) now take up to 5 returns to the tree with nothing affordable, where full-run salvage had hidden it at 3. The Advisor accepts 6 to 8 runs for the dearest node and says not to cut prices further, so the three tree/dry_runs are pinned at 5 and fall back inside the band when biome 2 gives those levels a better income. tideblade/hard/gull_rock fell to 10% for the same reason: less gold from the same first-time climb leaves the Hard replay a little under its band; it is pinned and is tuned with the Tideblade's own biome. The two 1,400 Archer Post nodes (Marksman, Burst fire) stay in the tier that opens at Gull Rock rather than a later biome, because the fork_feel cells judge the two Archer sides in the first five levels, and a node out of reach there would make the sides play the same.

fork_feel.first_level_note: Judged from this level on: at Outpost no fork node is affordable yet (the first costs 600 gold), so the two sides cannot differ there. A player who picks a side saves up for its chain.
fork_feel.how: per level and pillar, the larger of the gap in Keep health left (a share of full health) and in clear time (a share of the longer one) between the Volley side and the Sniper side, first attempts of the average bot: the two sides must feel different even where they win as often
